//: The gate, and only the gate. `npm run typecheck` runs this and CI runs it on every pull request — because nothing type-checked the renderer until v1.30.2, and two ReferenceErrors shipped through the gap: `I is not defined` in the panel's rail, `t is not defined` in the staging tree. What this has to catch is a name that does not exist and a call that cannot work.
//noUnused: Both ON since #83, and part of the gate now. The sweep that let them be turned on removed 163 dead declarations and surfaced three defects a type-checker sees and a reviewer does not: two icons that accepted a `size` and rendered without it, and a chevron given `open` that never turned — the CSS rule it needed was there, nothing applied the class. The judgement the old note described is real and has not gone away, so it is written down where the next sweep will look: an element of an ARRAY pattern leaves a HOLE (`const [, setA] = useState()`), because removing it rebinds the setter to the value; and a whole PARAMETER is never cut, since dropping one changes a signature. Both are why this is a gate and not a script.
//tests: The suites are compiled by ts-jest with tsconfig.jest.web.json, which is what `npm test` reports on. They also do on purpose what this config forbids — render a component with the three props a test needs rather than the thirty it declares — so checking them twice, by two different standards, only produces noise.
